concept.title: Set up and maintain the in-app help
concept.shortdesc: These docs live in the docs folder of the command-centre repository and publish to the OpenD site on every push. The app's help panel shows them for the page in use.

section.title: Server settings

property.propdesc: The docs site. Also the audience of embed tokens, so it must match the site's public URL exactly.
The app name in help-contexts.yaml and in each topic's resourceid appname.

The docs site's embed secret, at least 32 characters. With it, ? opens the side panel signed in as the current user. Without it, ? opens the help page in a new tab, where the docs site signs the reader in if it is private.
The OpenD organization slug the app's users are readers in, if they are registered in one.

section.p: On the docs site, add the app's origin (such as https://command.desktopmachineshop.com) to the embed origins, set the same embed secret, and register each user's email as a reader. A user the docs site doesn't know sees sign-in failed in the panel.

ol.li: Pick a key: the page's route (approvals), then dots for parts of it (approvals.revise). A key falls back to its parent until it has its own topic.
In the app, put data-help-key="approvals.revise" on the field, button or form, or data-help-pane on a tab, pane or dialog. New pages need a route in docs/help-contexts.yaml.
In the docs, tag the topic or a nested section with <resourceid appname="command-centre" appid="approvals.revise"/>.
Run pnpm --filter @cc/web help-topics to update apps/web/src/help-topics.json, the page each key opens in a new tab. A test fails while it is out of date.
Push. A build that fails validation never goes live, and the commit's opend/build status names the errors.
